_comment: ngsolve linear_elasticity#2 (gfu.components is a tuple of ComponentGridFunction views). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604, unit_square maxh 0.25, VectorH1 order 2 set from (x^2, -3y). The container's runtime type is exactly tuple and both elements are ComponentGridFunction; item assignment raises TypeError, which is the concrete consequence of 'NOT a list', exercised rather than asserted. Each component evaluates correctly at a mesh point (0.16 and -1.8 at (0.4,0.6)), each vector has the scalar space's 85 DOFs, and the two together account for the whole VectorH1 vector. They are views in both directions: adding 7 through a component moves the parent vector by exactly 7, and writing through the parent changes what the component evaluates to. Mutation: copying the component vector before writing breaks the aliasing and the fixture fails on component_is_a_view_not_a_copy. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable, INVERTED direction -- this fixture executes no pathology, so the control COMMITS the documented mistake instead of removing it): T2_MUTATE=1 copies the component vector (write_vec = comps[0].vec.CreateVector()) before the +7 is written into it, i.e. treats gfu.components[0] as a copy rather than a live view. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 8 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 prints parent_changed_by_component_write=0.000000 instead of 7.000000, so it removes 'component_is_a_view_not_a_copy=True' and makes the forbidden 'FAIL:' appear, and the fixture goes red. Observed while running the control: 'component_sees_parent_write=True' SURVIVES the mutation -- the parent write lands on DOF 0, whose basis function is identically zero at the probe point mesh(0.4,0.6), so that boolean is true whether or not the component sees the parent write. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py CAVEAT found while adding the mutation control (assertion NOT changed): 'component_sees_parent_write' is vacuous. The parent write gf.vec[0] -= 7.0 lands on dof 0, whose basis function evaluates to exactly 0.0 at the probe point mesh(0.4, 0.6) (measured: 0.20 elsewhere, 0.0 there), so the probe cannot see that write by construction. Under mutation a live -7 sits in the parent and the line still prints True; it passes unmutated only because the +-7 cancel. The parent-to-component direction is never tested. Comparing comps[0].vec[0] against gf.vec[0] would measure it directly. FIXED 2026-08-08 (assertion changed): component_sees_parent_write was abs(comps[0](mesh(0.4, 0.6)) - v0) < 1e-12 after gf.vec[0] -= 7.0. DOF 0's basis function is exactly 0.0 at that probe point (0.20 elsewhere), so the evaluation could not see the write by construction -- it printed True under T2_MUTATE=1 with a live -7 sitting in the parent, and unmutated only because the +7 and -7 cancelled. The parent-to-component direction was never tested. It now reads the component's OWN entry and requires that it moved by the same amount as the parent's, which is what 'a view' means; parent_write_moved_the_parent is asserted alongside so the premise cannot rot.
